newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai B shares closed up on Thursday on a technical rebound but trading remained sluggish on bearish market sentiment with the approach of China's National Day holiday, brokers said.
The index edged up 0.098 points or 0.20 percent to 48.662 points, on volume of 5.4 million shares worth $2.1 million. Of 41 B shares, 31 traded, with 13 up, seven flat and 11 down.
Brokers said that the market was still bearish without follow-up buying despite the technical rebound, after heavy losses over the past few days.
China's National Day holiday will last five days from September 28 to October 2. Trading will resume on October 3.

"Speculative institutional buying helped the rebound with selling pressure decreasing ahead of the holiday," one broker said. "No big gains or losses are expected, with investors staying on the sidelines before the holiday."

China Textile Machinery was the star on a rebound thanks to speculative buying, soaring $0.018 or 21.95 percent to $0.100, on volume of 5,100 shares. Shanghai Tyre & Rubber traded the most on speculative cross-trading, rising $0.004 or 1.60 percent to $0.254, on volume of 1.0 million shares.
Shanghai A shares rose on rumours the exchange had held a meeting of broker representatives this afternoon, brokers said. Exchange officials declined to comment.
The A index ended up 20.911 points or 2.39 percent at 896.620 points, on volume of 521.6 million shares worth 5.4 billion yuan. The SSE 30 rose 54.347 points or 2.32 percent to 2394.192 points.
Shanghai Steel Tube, yesterday's biggest loser, became the star on a technical rebound, surging 1.35 yuan or 30.00 percent to 5.85 yuan, on volume of 343,800 shares.
